name: SpQR: A Sparse-Quantized Representation for Near-Lossless LLM Weight Compression
problem: 3-4 bit quantization causes moderate-to-high accuracy loss, worst on the small (1-10B) models that edge deployment actually targets.
mechanism: Store the weights that cause the largest quantization errors (outlier weights) SEPARATELY in a sparse high-precision structure, and compress everything else to 3-4 bits. A sensitivity criterion identifies outlier weights per group; the sparse buffer is stored as indices plus FP16 values, so the bulk stays in dense low-bit form. The point is that the error contribution of a few weights is disproportionate to their count.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): first near-lossless compression across model scales; relative perplexity loss under 1% for LLaMA and Falcon; runs a 33B-parameter LLM on a single 24GB consumer GPU with no performance degradation and a 15% speedup. COMPRESSION RATIO: 3-4 bits per weight PLUS the sparse outlier buffer, so the effective bits-per-weight is above the nominal 3-4 - the outliers are not free. QUALITY COST: <1% relative perplexity, which is the strongest quality-cost figure any 3-4 bit method in this KB reports.
